tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (deciding safety of lifecycle policies, identifying at-risk images) with explicit trigger contexts covering ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner, direct pulls, and explicitly excludes out-of-scope contexts (push/pull auth failures, replication, scanning). It is concise, staying within a short paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks which images a lifecycle policy will delete or expire, whether it is safe to apply or keep a lifecycle policy, whether an image used by ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner or direct pulls is at risk, why an image disappeared from ECR, or to review lifecycle policies across repositories. Do not use for push or pull authentication failures, replication or pull through cache, image scanning findings, or ECS task failures unrelated to image availability.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into ECR-specific domain procedures (lifecycle policy previews, evidence tiers, verdict model) without explaining general concepts like what ECR or HTTP is. All content is specific to the ECR lifecycle domain and not generic knowledge.
tests.evidence: Answer one question precisely for an Amazon ECR repository: which images will the lifecycle policy remove at its next evaluation, and is any of them still in use or tagged as a release?

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tables (check matrix rows, API field lists, permission tables) are all pushed to references/ files and only summarized or linked in the body. Conditional branches (Step 3/4/5) link out to reference files rather than embedding full procedures.
tests.evidence: Load [ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md](references/ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md) and run its numbered procedure exactly: rules in rulePriority order...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies when to load it, e.g. tied to specific steps or trigger conditions.
tests.evidence: Load at Step 1. ... Load at Step 4, or section 6 at Step 6 when CloudTrail returned events. ... Load on AccessDenied. ... Load when a verdict is contested.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root in the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (permissions, push correlation rule, verdict assignment) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible areas like scope resolution describe principles and reasoning rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: A BatchGetImage, GetDownloadUrlForLayer, PutImage, InitiateLayerUpload, CompleteLayerUpload or BatchCheckLayerAvailability event within 60 seconds of that image's imagePushedAt is part of the push and MUST NOT count as a consumer pull.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill establishes a clear default (preview) with simulation as a fallback only when preview fails, not presenting multiple equal options.
tests.evidence: Preview is the source of truth. Try StartLifecyclePolicyPreview on every run. Only when it cannot complete, simulate, labelling every simulated number SIMULATED.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (resolve scope, preview, fallback simulate, cross-reference, assign verdicts, render report) applicable to any repository/policy, not a one-off declaration for a specific instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1. Resolve scope. Account, Region(s), repositories, draft policy if any, pull window.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: Critical Rules and inline notes throughout (push correlation rule, denied-is-not-empty, guardrail cancellation) function as a gotchas section documenting non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: Denied is not empty. AccessDenied, a guardrail cancellation, a throttled retry budget or a Partial scan is never reported as "no references found".

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides a report template reference and describes report structure requirements, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: Render from [report-template.md](references/report-template.md) with its ## headings in order, Scope through Next Steps...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the full template lives in references/report-template.md and is only described at a high level in the body.
tests.evidence: Expiring Images has one row per digest (Tags, Digest first 12 hex, Pushed, Last recorded pull, Claimed by rule, Action, Verdict, Evidence naming the tier); survivors are listed once below it.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-check validation step before presenting output, checking consistency of counts and completeness of verdicts.
tests.evidence: Self check before responding. The expiring image count is identical in Scope, Source of Truth, Expiring Images and the Rule by Rule total; the Check Matrix has exactly 15 rows; the rating appears once; every verdict row names its evidence tier.
